# Option reference

<!-- Generated by build/gen-options-doc from proto/config/table.odin. Do not edit: run "make docs". -->

noirvpn reads OpenVPN configuration files. This page lists the 325 options that
it knows: the options of OpenVPN 2.6 and 2.7, and the options that only noirvpn
has.

| Status | Count | What noirvpn does |
|--------|------:|-------------------|
| Supported | 123 | The option works as in OpenVPN. |
| New in noirvpn | 23 | The option does not exist in OpenVPN. |
| Not applied yet | 9 | noirvpn reads the option but does not use it yet. The note says if it warns or refuses to start. |
| Ignored | 57 | The option has no effect. noirvpn warns at start and in `--check-config`. |
| Rejected | 113 | noirvpn does not start. The error gives the reason and, if one exists, the replacement. |

The other columns:

- **Applies to**: `client`, `server` or `both`.
- **Arguments**: the number of arguments. `1-2` is one or two, `3+` is three or more.
- **Pushable**: a server can push the option to its clients.

An option that is not on this page is a start-up error. It becomes a warning if
the configuration lists the option in `ignore-unknown-option` or sets
`setenv FORWARD_COMPATIBLE 1`. To see what noirvpn does with each line of a
configuration, run `noirvpn --check-config --config FILE`.

How to use the options: [client configuration](client.md), [server
configuration](server.md) and [the tls transport](tls-transport.md).

## Supported

| Option | Applies to | Arguments | Pushable | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `allow-compression` | both | 1 |  | only the value no is accepted because compression has been removed |
| `askpass` | both | 0-1 |  | the passphrase of an encrypted key (key, tls-transport-key): the first line of the file, or typed at the terminal at start-up when no file is given |
| `auth` | both | 1 |  | digest for tls-auth; the data channel only uses AEAD |
| `auth-retry` | client | 1 |  | none, nointeract or interact |
| `auth-token` | client | 1 | yes | pushed by the server after authentication |
| `auth-token-user` | client | 1 | yes | pushed by the server with auth-token |
| `auth-user-pass` | client | 0-1 |  | send a username and password; the file contains them on two lines |
| `bind` | both | 0-1 |  | bind to a local address and port (the default for servers) |
| `block-ipv6` | both | 0 | yes | drop IPv6 packets at the tunnel, in both directions; no ICMPv6 reply is sent |
| `ca` | both | 1 |  | CA certificates (PEM) |
| `ccd-exclusive` | server | 0 |  | require a client-config-dir file for every client |
| `cd` | both | 1 |  | change directory before files are read; give an absolute path |
| `cert` | both | 1 |  | our certificate (PEM) |
| `client` | client | 0 |  | client mode: same as pull and tls-client |
| `client-config-dir` | server | 1 |  | directory of per-client config files |
| `client-to-client` | server | 0 |  | forward traffic between clients |
| `config` | both | 1 |  | include another config file |
| `connect-freq` | server | 2 |  | at most n new connections per sec seconds |
| `connect-freq-initial` | server | 2 |  | at most n initial replies per sec seconds (UDP) |
| `connect-retry` | client | 1-2 |  | seconds between connection attempts, and an optional cap for the back-off |
| `connect-retry-max` | client | 1 |  | number of attempts per remote before giving up |
| `connect-timeout` | client | 1 |  | seconds to wait for a server before trying the next one |
| `connection` | client | 0 |  | connection profile block: <connection> ... </connection> with one remote and its own options |
| `crl-verify` | both | 1-2 |  | revocation list: a file with CRLs in PEM (reloaded when it changes), or a directory (with the flag dir) with one file per revoked certificate, named by its serial number; checks the peer certificate chain (ca), not peer-fingerprint |
| `data-ciphers` | both | 1 |  | colon-separated AEAD ciphers in order of preference |
| `dev` | both | 1 |  | tun devices only; dev tap is rejected |
| `dev-type` | both | 1 |  | only tun is accepted |
| `dhcp-option` | client | 1-3 | yes | DNS servers and search domains for the tunnel |
| `disable` | server | 0 |  | refuse this client; only valid in a client config file |
| `disable-dco` | both | 0 |  | same as datapath userspace; conflicts with datapath dco, udco and auto; in a client service profile, the connections of that profile will run without DCO |
| `dns` | client | 1+ | yes | DNS settings for the tunnel |
| `duplicate-cn` | server | 0 |  | allow several sessions with the same identity |
| `explicit-exit-notify` | both | 0-1 |  | tell the peer when this side stops (UDP) |
| `extra-certs` | both | 1 |  | extra chain certificates to send |
| `float` | both | 0 |  | accept authenticated packets from a new peer address (server); a client shows a warning that it is not applied |
| `group` | both | 1 |  | switch to this group after start-up (Linux only) |
| `hand-window` | both | 1 |  | how many seconds a handshake may take |
| `http-proxy` | client | 2-4 |  | reach the remote through an HTTP CONNECT proxy: host port [authfile|auto] [none|basic]; only Basic authentication is supported |
| `http-proxy-option` | client | 1-3 |  | VERSION 1.0|1.1, AGENT string, CUSTOM-HEADER name content |
| `http-proxy-user-pass` | client | 1 |  | the credentials for `http-proxy host port auto` (file, or an inline block): user name on line 1, password on line 2 |
| `ifconfig` | client | 2 | yes | tunnel address and netmask; normally pushed by the server |
| `ifconfig-ipv6` | client | 1-2 | yes | tunnel IPv6 address; normally pushed by the server |
| `ifconfig-ipv6-pool` | server | 1 |  | set the dynamic IPv6 address range |
| `ifconfig-ipv6-push` | server | 1-2 |  | fixed IPv6 tunnel address for one client; only valid in a client config file |
| `ifconfig-noexec` | both | 0 |  | do not configure the interface; only report the settings on the bus |
| `ifconfig-pool` | server | 2-3 |  | set the dynamic address range (overrides the range derived from server) |
| `ifconfig-pool-persist` | server | 1-2 |  | remember client addresses in a file |
| `ifconfig-push` | server | 2-3 |  | fixed tunnel address for one client; only valid in a client config file |
| `ignore-unknown-option` | both | 1+ |  | do not stop with an error on these unknown options |
| `inactive` | both | 1-2 | yes | disconnect after n seconds without tunnel traffic; a client only applies it from its own config, and a server ignores it with a warning |
| `iroute` | server | 1-2 |  | subnet behind one client; only valid in a client config file or the peers file |
| `iroute-ipv6` | server | 1 |  | IPv6 subnet behind one client; only valid in a client config file |
| `keepalive` | both | 2 |  | ping interval and timeout; a server pushes them to clients |
| `key` | both | 1 |  | our private key (PEM) |
| `key-direction` | both | 1 |  | 0 or 1; selects which halves of the tls-auth key are used |
| `local` | both | 1-3 |  | local address, port and protocol (a server may list several) |
| `lport` | both | 1 |  | local port |
| `max-clients` | server | 1 |  | maximum number of concurrent clients (default 1024) |
| `max-packet-size` | both | 1 |  | control packet size limit; also sets mssfix |
| `max-routes-per-client` | server | 1 |  | maximum number of internal routes per client (default 256) |
| `mode` | both | 1 |  | only server is accepted; p2p is not supported |
| `mssfix` | both | 0-2 |  | clamp the TCP MSS of connections in the tunnel; N is the largest data channel packet, mtu: the largest outer IP packet, fixed: the largest inner packet |
| `multihome` | server | 0-1 |  | accepted but not needed, because a UDP server always replies from the address the client used; same-interface also replies through the interface the client used |
| `ncp-ciphers` | both | 1 |  | old name of data-ciphers |
| `nobind` | client | 0 |  | do not bind a local port |
| `peer-fingerprint` | both | 1+ |  | SHA-256 fingerprints of accepted peer certificates |
| `persist-tun` | both | 0 | yes | a client keeps its tun device, addresses and routes across reconnects; a server keeps its device for its whole run anyway |
| `ping` | both | 1 | yes | send a ping after n idle seconds |
| `ping-restart` | both | 1 | yes | restart after n seconds without receiving a packet |
| `ping-timer-rem` | both | 0 |  | run the ping timers only when a peer is known |
| `port` | both | 1 |  | local and remote port |
| `proto` | both | 1 |  | udp, tcp-client, tcp-server, tls-client or tls-server (TCP in an outer TLS stream, noirvpn to noirvpn), with 4 or 6 for one IP version |
| `proto-force` | client | 1 |  | only use remotes with this transport protocol |
| `pull` | client | 0 |  | accept options pushed by the server |
| `pull-filter` | client | 2 |  | accept, ignore or reject pushed options by prefix |
| `push` | server | 1 |  | send an option to clients |
| `push-remove` | server | 1 |  | drop matching pushed options for one client; only valid in a client config file |
| `push-reset` | server | 0 |  | drop all inherited pushed options for one client; only valid in a client config file |
| `rcvbuf` | both | 1 | yes | socket receive buffer size |
| `redirect-gateway` | client | 0+ | yes | send all IP traffic through the tunnel |
| `redirect-private` | client | 0+ | yes | like redirect-gateway, but the default route is not changed |
| `remote` | client | 1-3 |  | server host, port and protocol |

| `remote-cert-ku` | both | 0+ |  | the certificate of the peer must have a key usage with at least all the bits of one value (hex, 1 to ff, e.g. a0); with no value, it only needs to have a key usage |
| `remote-cert-tls` | both | 1 |  | the certificate of the peer must have a key usage and the extended key usage of a server (TLS Web Server Authentication) or of a client (TLS Web Client Authentication) |
| `remote-random` | client | 0 |  | shuffle the remote list at start-up |
| `reneg-bytes` | both | 1 |  | renegotiate after n bytes |
| `reneg-pkts` | both | 1 |  | renegotiate after n packets |
| `reneg-sec` | both | 1-2 | yes | renegotiate after at most max and at least min seconds |
| `resolv-retry` | client | 1 |  | seconds to retry name resolution, or infinite |

| `route-gateway` | client | 1 | yes | default gateway for routes |
| `route-ipv6` | both | 1-3 | yes | add an IPv6 route: prefix, gateway, metric |
| `route-ipv6-gateway` | client | 1 | yes | default gateway for IPv6 routes |
| `route-metric` | client | 1 | yes | default metric for routes |
| `route-noexec` | both | 0 |  | do not add routes; only report them on the bus |
| `route-nopull` | client | 0 |  | ignore pushed routes and DNS options |
| `route-table` | both | 1 |  | routing table id for routes (Linux) |

| `server` | server | 2-3 |  | server mode: network, netmask and optional nopool |
| `server-ipv6` | server | 1 |  | IPv6 network for the tunnel |

| `verify-client-cert` | server | 1 |  | require (default), or optional: a client without a certificate logs in with a user name and password (needs peer-passwords or auth-external), and any certificate that is sent must still pass. With no ca, peer-keys or peer-fingerprint, the server does not ask for a certificate at all and only accepts password logins. none is not supported |
| `verify-x509-name` | both | 1-2 |  | the certificate of the peer must have this name: the whole subject (type subject, the default), the common name (name) or the start of it (name-prefix); x509-username-field is not applied, so the common name is used |
| `writepid` | both | 1 |  | write the process id to this file |

## New in noirvpn

| Option | Applies to | Arguments | Pushable | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auth-external` | server | 0-1 |  | ask a bus controller to decide each session; optional timeout in seconds |
| `auth-web` | server | 0 |  | a client that sends IV_SSO=webauth with no certificate and no password waits while the controller handles a web sign-in (needs auth-external and verify-client-cert optional) |
| `bus-allow` | both | 3+ |  | map a uid, gid or SID to bus roles: bus-allow uid|gid|sid id role... |
| `bus-control` | both | 1-5 |  | control socket: off, or a path with optional mode and group |
| `bus-events` | both | 1-5 |  | events socket: off, or a path with optional mode and group |
| `client-service` | client | 0 |  | service mode: this config only holds service settings, and the profile is received over the control bus |
| `connect-freq-source` | server | 1 |  | at most n initial replies for one source address in the connect-freq-initial window (default 20; 0: no limit) |
| `datapath` | both | 1 |  | userspace, dco (the Linux ovpn kernel module), udco (a userspace DCO service) or auto (the kernel module if available, otherwise the service, otherwise this process) |
| `dco-socket` | both | 1 |  | socket of the DCO service for `datapath udco` or `auto` (default /run/udco/udco.sock) |
| `peer-keys` | server | 1 |  | peers file: one pinned key per line (username, pin, options) |
| `peer-keys-mode` | server | 1 |  | pin (default), both (chain and pin) or either (a pin, or else a chain); both and either need ca and peer-keys; ca with peer-keys and no mode is the same as either |
| `peer-passwords` | server | 1 |  | file of user names and password hashes; the server checks the password of a client against it; a password source for verify-client-cert optional |
| `pq-mode` | both | 1 |  | off, prefer (default) or require the hybrid post-quantum key exchange |
| `stats-interval` | both | 1 |  | publish a stats.tick bus event every n seconds (0 or not set: off) |
| `tls-transport-accept-tcp` | server | 0 |  | every proto tls-server listener also accepts raw OpenVPN tcp-client connections on the same port (identified by the first 3 bytes) |
| `tls-transport-cert` | server | 1 |  | certificate (leaf first, then the chain; PEM) for the outer TLS of proto tls-server; default: cert |
| `tls-transport-dev` | server | 1 |  | name of the second tun device for the proto tls-server clients under datapath dco or udco; default: the dev name with -tls added |
| `tls-transport-hello` | client | 1 |  | the ClientHello sent in the outer TLS of proto tls-client: default (what the TLS library sends) or chrome (Chrome's cipher list, signature algorithms, ALPN, session ticket and more, as far as the library allows); it also sets the headers of the WebSocket upgrade request with tls-transport-ws |
| `tls-transport-key` | server | 1 |  | private key (PEM) for the outer TLS of proto tls-server; default: key |
| `tls-transport-sni` | client | 1 |  | server name in the outer TLS of proto tls-client; default: the remote host name, none for an address |
| `tls-transport-strict` | client | 0 |  | refuse the connection when the outer TLS certificate does not match the server's key (which means another party terminates the outer TLS) |
| `tls-transport-ws` | both | 1 |  | send the tls transport in a WebSocket at this path: a tls-client sends the HTTP upgrade request, tls-server and tcp-server listeners respond to it (for a reverse proxy that terminates the outer TLS at the HTTP layer) |
| `workers` | both | 1 |  | crypto worker threads for the data channel (0 means none, the default; peers are spread across the threads) |

## Not applied yet

| Option | Applies to | Arguments | Pushable | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `capath` | both | 1 |  | not available yet (start-up error): use ca with one file |
| `data-ciphers-fallback` | both | 1 |  | not applied yet (no warning): the peers must negotiate an AEAD cipher |
| `mark` | both | 1 |  | not applied yet (warning): the firewall mark is not set on the socket |
| `mlock` | both | 0 |  | not applied yet (warning): memory is not locked |
| `mtu-disc` | both | 1 |  | not applied yet (warning): the path MTU discovery mode of the socket is not set |
| `ping-exit` | both | 1 | yes | not applied yet (warning): it only turns off the default ping-restart |
| `push-peer-info` | client | 0 |  | not applied yet (warning): no extra client details are sent |
| `replay-window` | both | 1-2 |  | not applied yet (warning): the default replay window of the data channel is used |
| `x509-username-field` | server | 1 |  | not applied yet (no warning): the client identity is the common name (CN) |

## Rejected (error)

| Option | Applies to | Arguments | Pushable | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `allow-deprecated-insecure-static-crypto` | both | 0 |  | static-key mode has been removed; use TLS |
| `allow-nonadmin` | both | 0-1 |  | the service decides who may connect (bus-allow sid) |
| `app-custom-control` | both | 1 |  | custom control messages are not supported |
| `auth-gen-token` | server | 0-3 |  | auth tokens are not issued; a controller decides each login on the control bus (auth-external) |
| `auth-gen-token-secret` | server | 0-1 |  | auth tokens are issued from external authentication on the control bus (auth-external) |
| `auth-user-pass-optional` | server | 0 |  | username checks are handled over the control bus (auth-external) |
| `auth-user-pass-verify` | server | 1-2 |  | scripts have been removed; use auth-external to decide over the control bus (auth.decide) |
| `bind-dev` | both | 1 |  | VRF binding is not supported |
| `chroot` | both | 1 |  | chroot is not supported; use the service manager or a container for isolation |
| `client-cert-not-required` | server | 0 |  | removed in OpenVPN 2.5; every client must present a certificate |
| `client-connect` | server | 1 |  | scripts have been removed; subscribe to the peer.connect bus event (noirvpn-hook); per-client settings go in client-config-dir, the peers file or auth.decide |
| `client-crresponse` | server | 1 |  | challenge and response are handled over the control bus (auth-external) |
| `client-disconnect` | server | 1 |  | scripts have been removed; subscribe to the peer.disconnect bus event (noirvpn-hook) |
| `client-nat` | client | 4 | yes | stateless NAT is not supported |
| `comp-lzo` | both | 0-1 | yes | compression has been removed; delete the line |
| `comp-noadapt` | both | 0 |  | compression has been removed; delete the line |
| `compat-mode` | both | 1 |  | peers older than OpenVPN 2.6 are not supported, so there is no compatibility mode |
| `compress` | both | 0-1 | yes | compression has been removed; delete the line |
| `cryptoapicert` | both | 1 |  | the Windows certificate store is not supported; put the certificate and key in the config |
| `dhcp-release` | both | 0 |  | the client sets the addresses itself; there is no DHCP |
| `dhcp-renew` | both | 0 |  | the client sets the addresses itself; there is no DHCP |
| `dns-updown` | client | 1+ |  | noirvpn applies DNS settings itself; they are in the client.tunnel_settings bus event |
| `down` | both | 1 |  | scripts have been removed; subscribe to the client.state and client.tunnel_settings bus events (noirvpn-hook) |
| `down-pre` | both | 0 |  | scripts have been removed; subscribe to the client.state and client.tunnel_settings bus events (noirvpn-hook) |
| `engine` | both | 0-1 |  | OpenSSL engines are not supported |
| `fragment` | both | 1-2 |  | internal fragmentation has been removed; use mssfix and tun-mtu |
| `genkey` | both | 1-3 |  | not a daemon option, and noirvpn does not generate keys; use your PKI tools, or openvpn --genkey for static and tls-crypt keys |
| `help` | both | 0 |  | this is a command-line flag, not a config option; run noirvpn --help |
